title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana provisioning for Private installs + upgrade/rollback tooling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Private (VPC/on-prem) installs previously required manual wiring for Prometheus, Grafana provisioning and log shipping. Customers and internal SREs repeatedly requested a reproducible automation path for observability that works with both the private-installer and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/Helm) workflows. This PR adds end-to-end automation for provisioning the observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana + Loki/Fluentd) for Private installs and introduces an opinionated upgrade/rollback helper for observability components.

What this PR includes: automated Helm values and chart defaults to provision Prometheus/Grafana in Private installs, Grafana provisioning for dashboards and data sources, Prometheus scrape jobs and ServiceMonitors for core Redwood services, a Terraform module to wire observability resources and IAM roles for cloud deployments, log shipping overlays (Loki + Fluentd) and a scripted upgrade/rollback helper to safely apply changes and revert if metrics/dashboards regress.

Key changes (high level): - redwood-private-installer/helm/values-observability.yaml: default values and toggles to enable/disable automated provisioning - redwood-private-installer/helm/templates/grafana-provisioning.yaml: provisions datasources & dashboards via provisioning API - redwood-terraform/modules/observability/: new module to create managed infra (S3/Blob buckets for remote write, IAM/service accounts) - redwood-private-installer/scripts/upgrade-observability.sh: idempotent upgrade path with pre/post checks and rollback staging - redwood-private-installer/kustomize/overlays/log-shipping/: Loki/Fluentd manifests and configs - observability-pack/dashboards/*: curated dashboards for latency, token usage, KV-cache hitrates

Checklist (developer): - [x] Helm values and chart templates tested locally with kind and with a VPC test cluster - [x] Terraform module tacked into the private-installer staging plan and smoke-tested - [x] Grafana provisioning loads dashboards automatically on first run - [x] Upgrade script exercises a full upgrade and rollback on staging cluster - [x] Documentation updated with enablement steps and tuning knobs

Backward compatibility and safety: defaults are OFF for existing customers. Enabling the automation is opt-in via installer flags or Terraform inputs. The upgrade script creates a safe staging namespace and performs health checks (Prometheus targets scraped, dashboards provisioned, critical alerts not firing) and will rollback the Kubernetes manifests and Helm releases if checks fail. The provisioning uses stable, versioned Grafana provisioning files so dashboard changes are explicit and reviewable.

Testing & validation: unit tests for templating, integration runs in our perf-canary private cluster (AWS VPC) and a bare-metal lab cluster. We validated log shipping at ~1000 EPS and Prometheus scrape targets ~200 with acceptable memory usage. See the testing_summary field for details.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the upgrade script idempotency, IAM assumptions in the Terraform module, and the Grafana provisioning template (ensure dashboards contain stable panel IDs).
commits: init: add observability helm values and templates
feat(terraform): add observability module with remote-write and storage bindings
chore(installer): wire terraform module into private-installer bootstrap flow
feat(scripts): add upgrade-observability.sh with pre/post health checks and rollback
test: add integration smoke tests for provisioning and log shipping
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Can the upgrade script run with --dry-run against an existing install? (author) Yes, added --dry-run and a --force flag for manual overrides.
Maya Singh: Terraform module assumes S3-compatible storage. Does it support Azure Blob? (author) Added storage_type input and an examples/azure.tf using azurerm storage-account and blob container.

Luca Rossi: Grafana provisioning will overwrite dashboards on re-provision. Please ensure idempotency. (author) Updated templates to use uid based provisioning files and preserved annotations to avoid accidental deletions.
QA (Jordan Blake): Observed intermittently failing integration test due to prometheus scrape timing; added a readiness probe to the Prometheus StatefulSet to reduce flakes.
testing_summary: Integration tested against two staging environments: AWS VPC cluster (k8s 1.25) and on-prem lab (k3s) between 2025-11-14 and 2025-11-18. Scenarios: fresh install with automated provisioning enabled; upgrade from previous chart version and rollback on injected failure; log shipping load test at 1k EPS; Prometheus scrape target load at 200 targets. Health checks verify Prometheus targets, rule eval success, Grafana provisioning API responses, and Loki ingestion. Metrics observed: CPU increase within expected bounds, Prometheus memory growth capped with remote_write enabled. Manual verification: dashboards load and panel data matches sources.
release_notes:
- Add opt-in automation for Prometheus/Grafana provisioning in Private installs
- New Terraform observability module (S3/Blob remote-write + access bindings)
- Log shipping overlays for Loki + Fluentd
- Upgrade/rollback script to safely apply observability changes
- Default automation OFF; enable via installer flag or terraform input
